name: Orthodontic mini-implants (TADs) for gummy smile
lead: Orthodontic mini-implants, also called temporary anchorage devices (TADs) or miniscrews, are small screws placed in the bone of the upper jaw to give orthodontists a fixed anchor point. For a gummy smile, where a lot of gum shows when smiling, they are used to push (intrude) the upper front teeth upward so that less gum is visible and the smile reads as more balanced.[1]

Published reports describe placing one or two miniscrews between or above the front teeth, or a screw in the midline of the palate, and attaching them to the braces so that the incisors, or the whole upper tooth segment, are moved up and slightly back.[1] Case reports describe patients whose high smile line and convex profile changed to an average smile line and a straighter profile.[1]
Because the screws are small and temporary, this approach is discussed as a braces-based alternative to gum surgery or jaw surgery for people whose gummy smile is related to tooth position.[1]

chain: Upper front teeth are intruded upward
angle.text: A mini-implant gives braces a fixed point to pull the upper front teeth upward, which lowers how much gum shows on a full smile. Orthodontists use single or double screws at the front of the arch or a midpalatal screw, and report the change within a regular course of braces.

card.summary: Small screws in the upper jaw anchor braces so the front teeth can be moved upward, reducing how much gum shows in a smile.
card.note: Done by an orthodontist as part of braces treatment.

quick.overview:
A mini-implant is a tiny temporary screw placed in the jawbone by an orthodontist. It acts as a fixed anchor so the upper front teeth can be pushed upward without pulling other teeth out of position.

For a gummy smile caused partly by how far the front teeth sit down relative to the gum, this lowers the teeth-and-gum relationship so less gum is visible. Published case series and trials report reduced gingival display and a lower overbite after intrusion.
quick.mechanism: The screw is attached to the braces wire or an elastic. Light continuous force draws the upper incisors, or the upper segment as a whole, upward and sometimes backward. Studies have compared one versus two front miniscrews, and also midpalatal screws that shift the whole upper bite plane upward.
quick.risks: Reported considerations in the orthodontic literature include screw loosening, irritation of the surrounding tissue, and the need for a candidate whose gummy smile is dental rather than caused by other factors. The screws are removed when treatment ends.

paras: A temporary anchorage device is a small screw placed in the alveolar bone or palate that serves as a stable anchor for orthodontic forces. Unlike conventional anchorage that relies on other teeth, a miniscrew does not itself move, so force can be directed at chosen teeth.[1]

For gummy smile, the target is the upper incisors or the upper front segment. Reports describe single miniscrews, double miniscrews placed on either side of the front teeth, and midpalatal miniscrews used with a modified transpalatal arch to shift the occlusal plane upward.[1]

A 2024 randomized clinical trial in Angle Orthodontist compared maxillary incisor intrusion with one versus two anterior miniscrews in people with a gummy smile, and a 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis in International Orthodontics compared single versus double miniscrew-assisted intrusion in gummy smile or deep bite.[1] Case reports describe total intrusion of the upper dentition in a skeletal Class II patient with severe gummy smile, upward movement of the occlusal plane using midpalatal miniscrews, and correction of excessive gingival display in a Class II Division 2 patient with temporary skeletal anchorage.[1] One study of upper incisor intrusion with miniscrews in Class II division 2 cases reported overbite falling from 6 mm to 1.8 mm.[1]

Gummy smile correction is discussed in appearance-improvement communities alongside gum contouring, lip repositioning and jaw surgery, with orthodontic intrusion described as the braces-based route for people whose teeth sit low relative to the gums.
